title: Pow(x, n)
keyIdea: Write n in binary. Square x over and over (x, x², x⁴, x⁸…) and multiply the answer by the powers whose bit is 1: x¹³ = x⁸ · x⁴ · x¹. That is about log₂ n steps. For negative n use 1/x, and keep n in a long long because −(−2³¹) overflows an int. Your version also uses long double for extra precision.

approaches.name: Binary exponentiation (double)
approaches.idea: The version I wrote first: the same loop with x and ans as double.
approaches.why: One loop step per bit of n; three variables.

approaches.name: Binary exponentiation (long double)
approaches.idea: Your code: num = n as long long, base = x as long double; flip base for negative n; while num > 0: if the low bit is 1, ans *= base; base *= base; num >>= 1. Return (double)ans.
approaches.why: One loop step per bit of |n|; long double gives extra precision through the squarings.
